body.x: In airports, hospitals and large public facilities, passengers and visitors who need mobility assistance must find their way through crowded, complicated indoor spaces. Moving a person from one point to another is only part of the job.
ALBA Robot, an autonomous mobility company based in Turin, Italy, has built its platform around the rest of it.

ALBA Robot, led by CEO Andrea Bertaia Segato, is presenting its autonomous personal mobility solutions at KES 2026, with the ALBA Ride platform for airports, hospitals and large public facilities. The company's goal is to meet Korean airports, healthcare institutions, smart-building operators and mobility companies and to explore proof-of-concept projects and local partnerships.

ALBA combines autonomous navigation with an intuitive digital interface so that people who need mobility assistance can move through complex indoor environments more independently. The company describes the platform as more than a self-driving wheelchair: with digital displays, computer vision and, in future, digital-twin applications, it can also act as a connected digital touchpoint within a facility, supporting the passenger experience, operational intelligence and digital media (DOOH) services.

ALBA's technology has been deployed in a real airport environment at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport in the United States, and its solutions have been introduced at Manchester Airport in the United Kingdom to support passenger mobility. The company has also developed airport and mobility projects in France, Italy, Switzerland and the United Arab Emirates.

In Asia, ALBA is developing opportunities in Korea, Japan and Singapore, and it regards Korea as particularly important because of its advanced airport infrastructure and its smart-city, healthcare, ICT and mobility sectors. It is looking for partners that can support local proof-of-concept projects and long-term market development, including airport and facility operators, mobility and ICT companies and system integrators. In Korea, the company plans to start by identifying PoC and operational opportunities in airports, hospitals and large facilities, then develop longer-term service models with Korean mobility and ICT companies.

ALBA names country-specific certification and regulatory requirements, building local technical support, integration with facility systems and finding reliable local partners as the main challenges in expanding abroad. The company says deployment depends on operations, maintenance and integration with each facility's existing environment as well as on the vehicle itself.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
